jobs.description:
Job Title

Director, Data Engineering Delivery

Job Description Summary

Reporting to the Global Head of Data Architecture & Engineering, the Director of Data Engineering Delivery will be a member of the Global Data Leadership team and will help shape data engineering strategy, standards, and execution across the organization. The role requires fluency with Databricks and the Azure ecosystem today, and the adaptability to evaluate and adopt additional data technologies as our platform evolves.

The Director of Data Engineering Delivery will be equally comfortable managing the deliverables and pipeline of work for a team of data engineers as they are building data platforms and developing the engineers who build on them. This is a hybrid technical and people leadership role: the successful candidate will lead, mentor, and grow a team of 5–8 data engineers and analysts whilst also contributing hands-on to data engineering deliverables on Databricks and Azure.

Job Description

Technical Leadership

Platform ownership: Lead the design, build, and continuous improvement of scalable data pipelines, Lakehouse architectures, and data products on Databricks and Azure, ensuring our engineering and architectural standards for performance, reliability, and cost are consistently delivered.
Hands-on contribution: Remain an active practitioner by contributing to high-impact pipelines, code reviews, architecture reviews, and complex troubleshooting.
Quality and governance: Champion data quality, observability, security, and governance practices, embedding them into the team’s engineering lifecycle and platform standards.

People Leadership

Team management: Directly manage a team of 5–8 data engineers, owning hiring, onboarding, performance management, compensation recommendations, and retention.
Coaching and development: Provide regular coaching, feedback, and career development planning for each team member, with clear growth paths for both individual contributor and leadership tracks.
Culture and engagement: Foster an inclusive, high-trust team culture grounded in psychological safety, technical curiosity, accountability, and continuous learning.

Project and Work Orchestration

Delivery ownership: Plan, prioritize, and orchestrate the team’s portfolio of data engineering work, ensuring on-time, on-quality delivery aligned with global data and business priorities.
Agile execution: Establish and refine agile delivery practices (intake, estimation, sprint planning, retrospectives) that balance discovery work, platform investment, and run-the-business commitments.
Risk and dependency management: Proactively identify, communicate, and resolve risks, blockers, and cross-team dependencies, escalating clearly and constructively when needed.
Operational excellence: Own production health for the team’s data products, including SLAs, on-call posture, incident response, and post-incident learning.

Stakeholder Management and Cross Team Collaboration

Business partnership: Build trusted relationships with business and technology stakeholders, translating their objectives into clearly scoped, prioritized data engineering outcomes.
Global team collaboration: Partner closely with peers across the Global Data Leadership team - architecture, data engineering, AI, governance, and product - to deliver cohesive, end-to-end data solutions.
Communication and storytelling: Communicate technical concepts, trade-offs, roadmaps, and progress effectively to audiences ranging from engineers to senior executives.

jobs.description:
Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

The Director of Metro Ethernet Engineering leads engineering, certification, deployment readiness, and lifecycle management for Lumen's Metro Ethernet platforms and services. This role translates approved network architecture into deployable engineering standards, validated configurations, implementation processes, operational tooling, and production-ready service offerings.

This leader manages a team of network engineers responsible for Metro Ethernet, PacketOptical networks and related operational ecosystems. The position serves as the primary engineering liaison between Network Architecture, Product, Planning, Operations, Systems Development, Testing, Service Delivery, and vendor partners. Responsibilities include technology qualification, hardware and software certification, service introduction, roadmap prioritization, risk management, operational readiness, and strategic investment planning for Metro Ethernet network evolution.

This role requires a strong, values-driven leader who builds trust, fosters teamwork, communicates with clarity and transparency, and keeps teams focused on customers and shared outcomes. The Director must translate complex technical strategy into clear direction, engage stakeholders across functions, develop talent, model accountability, and lead a high-performing engineering team through change, ambiguity, and transformation.

Location

This is a remote opportunity open to candidates located anywhere in the U.S.

The Main Responsibilities

Lead and develop a high-performing Metro Ethernet engineering team responsible for network technologies, platforms, service readiness, deployment standards, and lifecycle execution.
Provide technical leadership across Metro Ethernet, Packet Optical networks, MetRON, colorless networking, NID platforms, Ethernet services, coherent optics, routing, switching, and related access technologies.
Direct certification, qualification, interoperability testing, and production readiness for new hardware, software releases, optics, platforms, and network capabilities.
Own engineering execution of Metro Ethernet roadmap initiatives, including MetRON deployment, Metro 3.0 enhancements, Ethernet Fabric services, service automation, and next-generation access capabilities.
Translate architecture and strategy into engineering work packages, implementation plans, operational deliverables, standards, and repeatable deployment practices.
Partner across Architecture, Product, Planning, Operations, Systems Development, Testing, Service Delivery, and vendors to align priorities, resolve dependencies, and deliver customer-centered outcomes.
Serve as an engineering escalation leader for complex production issues, deployment challenges, technology limitations, and service-impacting events.
Build trust, communicate with clarity and transparency, foster teamwork and accountability, develop talent, and lead teams effectively through change, ambiguity, and transformation.

What We Look For In a Candidate

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Telecommunications, Computer Science, or related discipline.
10+ years of telecommunications or network engineering experience, including deep expertise in Ethernet networking, IP/MPLS, optical transport, routing, switching, and carrier network operations.
5+ years leading engineering teams, technical programs, or network technology initiatives, with demonstrated ability to develop talent, build trust, and lead through change.
Experience introducing network technologies from architecture through production deployment, including certification, vendor management, implementation planning, and operational readiness.
Strong program management, executive communication, stakeholder engagement, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Engineering or related technical discipline.
Experience with large-scale service provider Metro Ethernet networks and transformation programs.
Expertise in coherent optics, Ethernet access services, optical transport integration, automation platforms, assurance, activation, inventory, and operational support systems.
Familiarity with MEF, IEEE Ethernet standards, Y.1564, Y.1731, service assurance, and carrier Ethernet technologies.

The Senior Customer Technology Manager (CTM) is responsible for shaping the customer's future technology roadmap and translating customer needs into business opportunities, product requirements, and roadmap priorities.

Working at the intersection of customer technology strategy, business development, and product management, the CTM builds trusted relationships with customer stakeholders, identifies future challenges and opportunities, and drives adoption of ASML innovations. The role acts as the primary bridge between the customer and ASML's Business Lines, ensuring that customer requirements are understood, prioritized, and translated into compelling solutions.

The Senior CTM influences both customer technology decisions and ASML product development by aligning stakeholders around a common vision and creating business cases that accelerate technology adoption and customer value creation.

Roles and responsibilities

Customer Roadmap Enablement

Own the understanding of customer technology roadmaps, challenges, and future requirements.
Anticipate customer needs for future technology nodes and translate them into product and service requirements.
Drive customer adoption of new products, capabilities, and services by demonstrating technical and business value.
Assess technical feasibility, define customer-specific requirements, and support validation of new products and installed base solutions.
Shape customer technology strategies through active engagement with engineering, manufacturing, and technology management stakeholders.

Voice of Customer

Represent the customer's perspective within ASML and ensure customer requirements are reflected in product and service roadmaps.
Consolidate customer input and communicate roadmap priorities, capability gaps, and emerging opportunities to Business Lines and senior management.
Support executive engagements, including Technology Roadmap Meetings (TRMs), Executive Review Meetings (ERMs), and strategic customer discussions.
Identify portfolio gaps and advocate for investments that address future customer needs.

Business Development

Identify and develop new business opportunities by connecting customer challenges with ASML's technology portfolio.
Build business cases that demonstrate the value of new products, services, upgrades, and productivity improvements.
Collaborate with Account Managers, Service teams, Applications, and Product Management to drive opportunity creation and technology adoption.
Support negotiation of technical specifications, performance requirements, and customer-specific solution configurations.

Stakeholder Management

Build trusted relationships with customer stakeholders from technical experts through senior management.
Influence decision-making across customer organizations and within ASML.
Lead cross-functional teams across Business Lines, Customer Support, Applications, Product Management, Service, and Sales.
Facilitate alignment between customer priorities and ASML strategic objectives.

Customer Success

Ensure customer technology requirements are understood, translated, and successfully implemented.
Monitor customer satisfaction related to product performance, roadmap alignment, and technology adoption.
Support successful technology node transitions and introduction of new products and services.

Axos is a rare environment: the scale of a major bank, the velocity of a fintech, and direct executive authority over both the strategy and the delivery of a 400+ engineer organization. You'll join as Axos's AIDLC moves from pilot to competitive advantage, and you'll be the leader who sets the direction and makes it real across Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based delivery. Collaborate with product leadership to create a planning model where engineering strategy, constraints, and AI-enabled delivery capacity are upstream inputs to roadmap decisions.

Track record of setting multi-year technology or engineering strategy for a large development organization, including build-versus-buy and platform investment decisions.

About This Job

This role reports onsite to Axos Bank's HQ in San Diego, CA. Remote work is not available.

The SVP, Head of Engineering is the senior engineering leader for Axos's Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based development organizations: four engineering groups totaling 400+ engineers, spanning software development, quality assurance, and business analysis across customer-facing web and mobile applications as well as back-office applications. This is a hands-on technical leadership role as much as a strategic one. This leader sets the multi-year development strategy and application architecture direction for these organizations, and is just as comfortable stepping personally into a struggling delivery to diagnose the problem and get it back on track. They own the operating model that makes delivery predictable, partner with the Centers of Excellence to bring AI-driven delivery (AIDLC) into day-to-day work, and hold the quality bar for every customer-facing experience these teams ship.

Axos Bank is a federally chartered, digital-first bank with over $28B in assets and no physical branches. Every customer interaction across our Consumer and Securities segments happens through software these teams build and own. We move with the urgency of a fintech and the stability of a regulated institution, and we're at a pivotal moment of scale: investing heavily in AI-driven delivery and seeking the engineering leader who will set the strategy and define how these teams deliver in Axos's next chapter.

Why Join Axos:

Axos is a rare environment: the scale of a major bank, the velocity of a fintech, and direct executive authority over both the strategy and the delivery of a 400+ engineer organization. You'll join as Axos's AIDLC moves from pilot to competitive advantage, and you'll be the leader who sets the direction and makes it real across Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based delivery. If you're motivated by setting strategy, staying technical, and building something consequential you can measure in outcomes, this is an exceptional opportunity.

Target Range:

$240,000.00 /Yr. - $325,000.00 /Yr.

Actual starting pay will vary based on factors including, but not limited to, geographic location, experience, skills, specialty, and education.

Responsibilities:

Development Strategy & Technical Direction

Own the multi-year engineering and technology strategy for the Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based development organizations, translating business priorities into technical roadmaps.
Own application architecture and engineering standards across your four engineering groups, replacing legacy technical debt with modern, maintainable patterns such as API-first design and service-oriented design.
Set the technology and tooling direction for your organization, ensuring teams build on modern, well-supported platforms that scale, run reliably at low latency, and support 24x7 uptime.
Keep your organization on the cutting edge of relevant technology, evaluating and adopting new tools, frameworks, and architectural patterns ahead of the industry curve rather than after they become standard.
Make build-versus-buy and platform investment decisions for your organization, weighing speed, cost, and long-term technical health.
Partner with peer technology verticals to implement the platform and tooling infrastructure AIDLC requires at scale in a regulated banking environment.
Maintain a 12 to 24 month delivery capacity outlook for your organization that informs product roadmap feasibility and planning.

Delivery Leadership & Organizational Management

Lead, develop, and hold accountable the engineering leaders of the Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based development organizations.
Own delivery predictability as an organizational capability, improving the cadences, rituals, and accountability structures that make on-time, on-scope delivery the norm across these four groups.
Define and operate cross-team dependency management: surface coupling risks across co-dependent platforms within your organization and resolve conflicts before they become delivery failures.
Build and maintain engineering culture, career frameworks, and talent standards across development, QA, and BA disciplines, in partnership with HR and the Centers of Excellence.
When a critical delivery is off track, personally step in: assess the technical blockers, work directly with the engineers and leads involved, and make the technical and organizational calls needed to get it back on schedule. This is a roll-up-your-sleeves role, not a delegate-and-monitor one.

AI Driven Software Delivery

Bring Axos's AIDLC roadmap to life within your four engineering groups, moving beyond AI-assisted coding to autonomous agents that participate in building, testing, reviewing, and shipping software.
Measure the impact of AIDLC tooling in delivery terms, such as cycle time, defect escape rate, engineer throughput, and time-to-production.
Surface and resolve gaps between enterprise AI tooling standards and what your teams need in live delivery.
Enable Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces across your platforms, for internal agentic tooling and for external-facing integrations, as Axos extends AI access to its systems.

Quality & Customer Experience Standards

Set and enforce the engineering quality bar across customer-facing web and mobile platforms as well as back-office applications for the Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based organizations.
Own performance standards for these platforms. Low-latency response times, reliability SLAs, accessibility compliance, and UX consistency are delivery criteria, not aspirational targets.
Build QA and performance testing into the delivery pipeline as a continuous, automated function, not a gate at the end. Champion shift-left testing and AI-augmented quality practices across all four groups.
Establish and track customer-facing performance benchmarks, using data to drive engineering investment decisions and communicate quality posture to Jonathan and other stakeholders.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with shared-capability leaders in architecture, DevOps, security, QE tooling, and AIDLC infrastructure to ensure those capabilities are roadmapped to support your teams' delivery.
Collaborate with product leadership to create a planning model where engineering strategy, constraints, and AI-enabled delivery capacity are upstream inputs to roadmap decisions.
Represent your engineering organization in senior leadership conversations, translating strategy, delivery health, technical risk, and capability investment needs into business terms that feed directly into Jonathan's regular board-level reporting.
Partner with Risk, Compliance, and the CISO to ensure AIDLC and AI-driven delivery practices in your organization meet regulatory standards appropriate for a federally chartered bank.

Bachelor's degree in related field or higher.
10+ years of engineering leadership experience, including direct leadership of development, QA, and/or business analysis organizations of 300+ people.
Deep, hands-on technical background, including current fluency in modern application architecture and technology such as API-first design, microservices, Redis, and CI/CD: someone who has personally written production code or led technical implementation, and can credibly evaluate and challenge technical decisions rather than only manage the people who make them.
Deep working knowledge of how modern financial infrastructure operates, including banking and securities cores, fiat and securities settlement, and crypto and blockchain systems, along with a genuine willingness to rapidly learn as this technology continues to evolve.
Direct, personal experience leading major project delivery rescue: has stepped into a failing initiative themselves and turned it around, not only delegated the turnaround to others.
Track record of setting multi-year technology or engineering strategy for a large development organization, including build-versus-buy and platform investment decisions.
Demonstrated track record of building or transforming delivery operating models at scale, with measurable improvements in velocity, predictability, or quality attributable to organizational and process changes you led.
Hands-on experience with AI tooling in the AIDLC, having moved beyond AI-assisted development to deploying autonomous or semi-autonomous agents in testing, code review, or requirements workflows.
Deep expertise building and operating customer-facing digital products where performance, latency, and experience quality are primary engineering concerns.
Experience in a regulated industry with direct accountability for delivery practices that meet compliance and audit requirements.

Background in financial services, fintech, digital banking, payments, or wealth management technology.
Experience managing business analysis as an organizational function, with an understanding of how BA quality upstream affects delivery quality downstream.

Experience managing delivery across co-dependent, multi-platform environments where release sequencing and dependency management are first-class engineering concerns.
